note: HOLDOUT SPEND FREEZE (CLAUDE.md rule 22). A freeze is a SUSPENSION of the authorization that a calibration-complete marker grants, not a withdrawal of the marker itself. While `active` is true, NO out-of-training year may be solved, scored, or registered for ANY ISO — validation tier (2022 and any backward extension) and locked test (2019, H1-2026) alike — even with `--holdout-authorized` and a `complete` marker present. It is deliberately ADDITIVE and backward-compatible: `calibration-complete.json` is untouched, so every already-registered out-of-training bundle stays CI-legal and no prior one-shot is invalidated or re-armed. Enforced at the solve entry point by `scripts/run_calibration_full.py::enforce_holdout_year_gate`, which reads this file BEFORE the marker check and fails closed. Data intake for out-of-training windows is NOT frozen (rule 22 channel 1: intake is no-LP and remains permitted under session-logged owner authorization). Lifting the freeze is an owner action: set `active` to false and record the lift in `history` with the reason.
lift_scope: NARROW AND SPENT IN-SESSION. The owner lifted the freeze on 2026-08-05 for exactly one purpose: the PJM and NEISO 2022 VALIDATION touchpoints, each solved with its ISO's frozen keeper recipe. Nothing else was authorized and nothing else was spent — not 2018/2020/2021 (the backward ladder rungs), not 2019 or H1-2026 (locked tier, and `final` is still empty), and not any other ISO (CAISO/ERCOT/MISO hold no marker; NYISO holds one but was not run). The freeze is RE-ARMED in the same session immediately after the two spends land, so this `active: false` state is transient by design and the file's steady state remains frozen. The still-open CAMPD economic-layup residual that caused the freeze is NOT resolved — see `reason` — so a 2022 miss in either ISO must be read against a known-imperfect availability envelope, which is exactly what the touchpoint reports record.

scope.years: every year outside the 2023-2025 calibration window

reason: The CAMPD unit-outage detector books sustained economic layup as mechanical outage in ALL SIX ISO extracts (neiso-63, 2026-07-24; evidence results/calibration/FINDING-neiso63-campd-economic-layup-2026-07.md). Every ISO books 23-46% of its CC capacity-year as outage against a real EFOR+planned norm of ~10-15%. The availability envelope every keeper is calibrated against is therefore about to change materially. A validation or locked-test year scored now would be measuring the wrong fleet: a MISS would be uninterpretable (detector defect or genuine forecast error?) and a PASS would be actively misleading, because the locked tier is touch-once and cannot be re-scored after the fix lands. Freezing preserves the out-of-sample years as usable evidence instead of spending them on a known-defective input.
lifts_when: The merit-order-guard fix charter (docs/handoffs/campd-economic-layup-fix-charter-2026-07.md) reaches a decision — either the corrected detector is adopted and each affected ISO's keeper is re-audited on the corrected envelope, or the charter is closed with cause and the extract is confirmed fit for purpose. The owner lifts the freeze explicitly; no session lifts it by inference from a passing metric.
